definitions.explanation: A strip of cloth tied around the head. Worn as a symbol of effort, determination, or team spirit during festivals, sports events, studying, and manual labor.

examples.japanese: {運動会|うんどうかい}で{赤|あか}い{鉢巻|はちまき}をした{子供|こども}たちが{走|はし}っている。
examples.english: Children wearing red headbands are running at the sports day.

examples.japanese: {受験|じゅけん}{勉強|べんきょう}に{気合|きあい}を{入|い}れるため、{鉢巻|はちまき}を{巻|ま}いて{机|つくえ}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: To fire myself up for exam studying, I tied on a headband and sat down at my desk.

notes:
USAGE:
{鉢巻|はちまき} is deeply associated with determination and effort in Japanese culture. It is worn to show that one is serious and focused.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉢巻|はちまき}を{締|し}める (to tie a headband)
- {鉢巻|はちまき}を{巻|ま}く (to wrap/put on a headband)
- {鉢巻|はちまき}を{外|はず}す (to take off a headband)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{鉢巻|はちまき} are commonly seen at:
- {祭|まつ}り (festivals) — worn by participants carrying portable shrines
- {運動会|うんどうかい} (school sports days) — in team colors
- {受験|じゅけん} (exam preparation) — as a symbol of dedication
- {応援|おうえん} (cheering) — with slogans like {必勝|ひっしょう} (certain victory) written on them
